decisions.reason: As a newly launched product with its own dedicated page, it likely sits above the firm's initial aspiration level under uncertainty, so a medium-sized software firm would usually continue observing it rather than withdraw it quickly.

Although still early and likely facing uncertain demand, the dedicated presentation suggests enough internal commitment and expected fit with the firm's portfolio to justify keeping it for another period.
Its own page indicates active market positioning, and with limited post-launch feedback a boundedly rational firm would usually retain it while learning unless results clearly disappoint.

Because it was only mentioned on the website and appears close to other overlapping tariff tools, management would be more likely to see it as underperforming or redundant and reallocate resources elsewhere.

The standalone page suggests the firm sees this tool as strategically useful within the wider location and tariff offering, so available organisational slack supports keeping it despite early uncertainty.
Its weaker website prominence and strong overlap with the other energy comparison products make it a plausible candidate for problemistic search and withdrawal if it has not met initial aspirations.
